items.title: Hollywood fights AI in public while quietly building it into movies
items.summary: Data-driven report: the Times scraped about 250 public job postings at seven major studios in late June 2026 and judged about 30 AI-connected. Disney, Netflix and Amazon postings pointed to AI workflows for VFX, animation, sound and dubbing; others to marketing/analytics. Contrasts studios' public caution (lawsuits, union deals) with quiet internal adoption; notes Amazon commissioned three AI animation series and SAG-AFTRA's new protections.

items.event: Is AI-generated Animation Disrupting the Traditional Film and Television Industry?
items.title: The State of VFX and Animation Might Surprise You
items.summary: Column by the founder of HDRI Intelligence presenting the 2026 Visual Effects & Animation World Atlas. Argues that by mid-2026 AI had not replaced a significant number of roles at traditional VFX/animation studios; global headcount roughly flat over three years (+2.7% in past 12 months), LA −1.5%, US animation studios smaller on average; attributes shifts mainly to audience tastes, business strategy and tax incentives as well as technology. Answers Katzenberg's 2023 prediction with 'Not yet.'

items.title: ‘Critterz’ First Look: New Tech Behind AI Animated Feature Unveiled as Vertigo and Federation Form New AI Production Company (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary: Trade exclusive: first-look still from the AI-created animated feature Critterz (launching in the Cannes market via AGC Studios) and launch of amersia, an 'AI-native' production company from Vertigo Films and Federation Studios, with its production technology Woven. Largely company statements framing AI as human-led.

items.event: Is AI-generated Animation Disrupting the Traditional Film and Television Industry?
items.title: AI Dominates Cannes Buzz as Filmmakers Grudgingly Accept It: ‘You Probably Will Be Able to Make Something That Looks Like a Marvel Movie in Your Basement’
items.summary: Festival analysis: AI shifted from being cast as destructive to being grudgingly accepted at Cannes 2026. Cites Demi Moore, market titles using AI as a selling point (incl. Critterz), producers seeing cost savings, and festival director Thierry Frémaux calling for legislation. The author asserts animation/VFX job losses are a 'virtual certainty' and already happening, without citing data.

items.title: Amazon MGM Studios Embraces AI: Greenlights Three Series for Prime Video Under New ‘GenAI Creators’ Fund’
items.summary: Amazon MGM Studios and AWS launch the GenAI Creators' Fund and Project Nara AI production platform; three animated series greenlit for Prime Video. Adds interview material: Cheng calls the approach 'human-centric', says Nara promises lower costs and faster production, pilots had a five-week deadline, and human actors and voice actors are used.

items.title: Prime Video Orders Three GenAI Animated Series From New Amazon MGM Studios-AWS Creators’ Fund
items.summary: Same Amazon announcement: three animated series ordered via the GenAI Creators' Fund, powered by Project Nara. Reproduces the press-release quote from Albert Cheng and the loglines; adds that Cannes showed growing AI acceptance in animation/VFX and that new WGA and SAG-AFTRA deals eased strike fears.

items.title: The Animation Guild Shares ‘Generative AI’ Economic Impact Study Results
items.summary: Republishes The Animation Guild's key findings from CVL Economics' 'Future Unscripted' study (300 entertainment executives/managers, Nov–Dec 2023): 75% said GenAI had supported job elimination, reduction or consolidation; about 21.4% (~118,500) of US film, TV and animation jobs projected to be consolidated, replaced or eliminated by 2026.
